title: Informal Resolution Eligibility After Mandatory Reporter Disclosure Gap
scenario_text:
**Maxient Case #IX-2026-0052**
Complainant: Student E | Respondent: Faculty Member F (tenured, Chemistry Dept)
Disclosure to mandatory reporter: October 3, 2025 | Report filed by mandatory reporter: October 7, 2025
Formal complaint filed by Student E: January 14, 2026
Status: Complainant requesting informal resolution

**Email — Subject: "Mandatory reporter filing" (Oct 7, 2025)**
From: prof.kwame.asante@brightpath.edu
To: titleix@brightpath.edu
"Student approached me after class on 10/3 to disclose an incident involving a faculty member. Per my obligations I am reporting. Student expressed preference for confidentiality and stated they do NOT wish to file a formal complaint at this time. I informed them of their rights and provided the Title IX office contact."

**Canvas LMS — Course: CHEM 301, Fall 2025**
Instructor: Faculty Member F
Roster: Student E enrolled (dropped 10/15/25, processed via registrar as "late drop with W")
Grade at drop: B+

**Banner SIS — Student E transcript**
Fall 2025: CHEM 301 — W (withdrawn) | Spring 2026: CHEM 301 — enrolled (different section, Instructor: Prof. Patel)

**Google Doc — "BSU Title IX Policy v6.0" Section 11.3: Informal Resolution**
"Informal resolution is available for all formal complaints EXCEPT: (a) complaints involving an employee respondent and a student complainant where the employee had direct instructional or supervisory authority over the student at the time of the alleged conduct."

**Slack — #title-ix-deputies (Jan 16, 2026, 3:30 PM)**
@mark.innis: Diana — Student E case. They want IR. Faculty respondent but student dropped the course before filing. Does 11.3(a) exclusion still apply? They're not currently in respondent's class.
@diana.marchetti: What matters is "at the time of the alleged conduct" — when did the incident occur?
@mark.innis: Disclosure to Asante was 10/3, but student hasn't specified exact incident date yet. Could be during the enrollment period or before.
@diana.marchetti: We need the incident date nailed down before we can determine IR eligibility. Don't offer it yet.
[Thread continues 2 days later]
@mark.innis: Got it. Student confirms incident occurred September 22, 2025. They were enrolled in F's section at that time.
[No reply from diana.marchetti — but a :no_entry: emoji reaction added Jan 18]

**Google Calendar — "IR Eligibility Consult" (Jan 20, 2026, 11:00 AM)**
Required: diana.marchetti (accepted), mark.innis (accepted), university-counsel@brightpath.edu (tentative — never confirmed)
No meeting notes. No follow-up email.

**Maxient — Case #IX-2026-0052 (updated Jan 22, 2026)**
Case note by D. Marchetti: "IR ineligible per 11.3(a). Notifying complainant of formal process options only. Respondent had direct instructional authority at time of conduct (confirmed enrolled CHEM 301, incident 9/22/25)."
question: Student E's advisor appeals the IR eligibility determination, arguing that since Student E voluntarily dropped the course and is no longer under Faculty Member F's authority, the power dynamic no longer exists and informal resolution should be available. What is the correct institutional response?

contributor.name: Diana Marchetti
contributor.title: Title IX Coordinator
contributor.domain_expertise: Due process requirements, procedural versioning (pre/post 2022 regs), evidence standards, cross-campus jurisdiction

choices: IR is available because the mandatory reporter's filing on October 7 did not constitute a formal complaint — the formal complaint was not filed until January 14, 2026, by which time the instructional relationship had ended, and the policy should be read as of the complaint filing date.

IR remains ineligible — Section 11.3(a) explicitly keys the exclusion to 'at the time of the alleged conduct,' the incident occurred September 22 while Student E was enrolled in Faculty Member F's course, and the current enrollment status is irrelevant to the eligibility determination.
The determination is premature because university counsel's attendance at the January 20 consult was never confirmed, meaning the eligibility decision was made without required legal review.

The appeal has merit — the policy's purpose is to protect against coercion from power imbalances, and since Student E voluntarily left Faculty Member F's course, the rationale for the 11.3(a) exclusion no longer applies and IR should be offered.
